prerequisites: basic knowledge in the development and use of databases

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module know various ways to formally describe facts and know the concepts of logic programming.
Students who have successfully completed this module can use propositional logic and predicate logic for specification and can systematically derive logical consequences.
Students who have successfully completed this module can formalize logical relationships and can program with logical rules.
Students who have successfully completed this module can formalize logical relationships and can implement them in programs using logical rules.
Students who have successfully completed this module can distinguish informal from formal arguments and explain the differences.
Students who have successfully completed this module can assess the applications of deductive systems and evaluate the limits of logic applications.

syllabus_topics: Syntax and semantics of propositional logic
Syntax and semantics of predicate logic

assessment_methods.method: experimental work (weekly problem sets with exercises)

assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either an oral examination or a term paper of at least 15 pages. The ungraded assessment is experimental work consisting of weekly problem sets with exercises.
